text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [INCIDENT] STREAMING LATENCY SPIKE detected in prod us-west-2 for /v1/generate-stream at 2026-03-15T14:12:01Z (thread_ts 2179004321). p95 jumped from ~110ms to ~820ms, p99 to ~3.1s. Streaming stalls reported, error surface shows elevated tail latency and increased time-to-first-token for long responses.

Alex: seeing a huge jump in prefix cache miss ratio starting ~14:09. global_prefix_hitrate dropped from 0.87 -> 0.12 in under 3m. KV fetch latency spiked and we see GC-like paging on several shards.

Marina: I rolled prefix-hash v2 at 14:05 (intended to reduce key cardinality). Canary 10% at 14:05, expanded to 100% at 14:08 by the rollout automation.

Tom: confirm rollout commands (from CI):
```
# rollout log
./deploy --service=prefixhash --version=v2 --strategy=canary --percent=10 --started=2026-03-15T14:05:12Z
# automation then scaled to 100% at 14:08:03Z
```

deploy-bot: rollout completed: prefixhash v2 -> 100% at 2026-03-15T14:08:03Z (CI run 4832).

Alex: looks like v2 changed the salt and hash function (murmur3_64 -> xxhash64) which redistributed keys and created hot cold-shards; eviction pressure skyrocketed. Our streaming runtime depends on high prefix locality for KV cache. When misses spike, we do sync IO to backing store and streaming stalls.

infra-bot: paging alerts: kernel page faults up 6x on pod pool streamer-*/us-west-2 between 14:09-14:15.

sri: I'm taking primary pager. Immediate mitigation plan:
1) pause/rollback prefix-hash rollout to v1
2) add routing fallback to model-compact for affected routes to reduce streaming tail
3) increase prefetch window and async warmup of KV cache for hot prefixes
4) notify affected customers + open SEV channel

jess: pinging support to notify top customers (AcmeCorp, BetaApps). Acme on a live demo, they reported stalls/partial streams. Sending coordinated message now.

support-bot: customer-impact: AcmeCorp (3 calls) degraded p99 ~4s, BetaApps intermittent stalls, internal synthetic checks started failing at 14:11.

Marina: rolling back to v1 now. Command: `./deploy --service=prefixhash --to v1 --force`

deploy-bot: rollback triggered at 2026-03-15T14:18:20Z. Automation is reverting canary artifacts and reloading v1 mapping.

Alex: while rollback is in progress, we should enable immediate per-request fallback to model-compact to keep streaming responsive. Patch in runtime: set `fallback_model=redwood-13b-compact` for /v1/generate-stream for 30m.

Tom: applied fallback routing at 14:20:10Z. Also increased prefetch concurrency from 8 -> 24 for streaming pods to warm caches faster. Commands run: 
```
# runtime change
curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/routes/fallback -d '{"route":"/v1/generate-stream","fallback":"redwood-13b-compact","ttl":1800}'
# prefetch concurrency tweak
kubectl set env deployment/streamer PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=24 -n prod-usw2
```

Alex: after enabling fallback + prefetch, early signals show p95 dropped to ~150ms at 14:26, p99 ~620ms. Cache hitrate climbing back toward 0.6.

incident-bot: pager note: mitigation actions at 14:20-14:26 reduced customer impact; continue monitoring.

sri: asking infra to run targeted cache-warm job on affected prefixes (hotlist from query logs). Marina/ Alex coordinate.

Marina: kicked off warmup job at 14:28:45Z. Script warms KV for top-10k prefixes, batches 512 keys per pod. Logs: `warmup: 10k keys enqueued, expected runtime ~6m`

infra-bot: warmup job succeeded at 14:35:10Z. Observed local cache occupancy up 4x on streamer pods.

Alex: final metrics after rollback+fallback+warmup: p95 = 120-160ms, p99 = 480-700ms (gradually stabilizing). No new 5xx spikes. Streaming stalls largely resolved.

jess: customer comms updated: AcmeCorp notified of mitigation and that we're rolling back change and doing RCA. BetaApps given ETA for full stability (15:10).

support-bot: all impacted customer threads opened: INC-10021 (AcmeCorp), INC-10022 (BetaApps). No data exfiltration, not a security incident.

sri: handoff summary for second-shift SREs / postmortem owners:
- Incident: high streaming tail latency due to prefix-hash v2 rollout causing KV cache locality loss and cache miss surge -> page faults -> streaming stalls.
- Time window: 14:09 - 15:10 (mitigation actions began 14:18, rollback finished 14:35, full stabilization ~15:10).
- Impact: p95 from ~110ms -> ~820ms, p99 peaked ~3.1s, major customers saw degraded streams.
- Actions taken: rollback to v1, enable fallback routing to compact model, increase prefetch concurrency, run cache warmup, notified customers, opened incident tickets.
- Owner for RCA/postmortem: alex (eng-runtime).
- Follow-ups: revert rollout gating to require manual approval for any hash changes, add chaos tests for prefix redistribution, improve canary expansion automation to wait 30m before 100% expansion, add histogram alerts for prefix hitrate thresholds.

Alex: I'll own RCA and proposed fixes: 1) add canary guardrail to block full expansion if global_prefix_hitrate drops >10% vs baseline; 2) instrument per-shard eviction telemetry; 3) add automated warmup when hash mapping changes detected.

Marina: note — our change log: v2 intended to reduce entropy but used different seed ordering; need to document and test mapping differences.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED at 2026-03-15T15:12:01Z (last_message_ts 2179007921). Assigning follow-up owner tags.

sri: leaving final notes in #postmortems and assigning jira RED-INC-432 for full RCA. Handoff to Marina as secondary for rollout process improvements.

jess: will send a short customer-facing post-incident email after RCA draft.

Tom: captured logs and diagnostic bundle: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2179004321_bundle.tar.gz

Alex: thanks everyone — good mitigation work. We'll sync tomorrow for RCA. :thumbsup:
